messages:
Alex: Heads-up: production serving cluster r-4 seeing rapid OOM spikes on small-batch LLM endpoints (p95 latency stable but OOMs increasing since 10:12 UTC). Memory climbs ~200MB per minute then recovers, repeated. Likely KV cache thrash + kernel memory blowouts. @OpsOnCall can you take?
OpsOnCall: On it. switching traffic to fallback pool now. which model should we route to? canary to smaller quantized?
Alex: Route to 'rw-small-q4' for canary. Also capture a quick profile: enable RT_VERBOSE_KV=1 and grab kernel selection traces on one effected node (sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -f > /tmp/trace.log).
CI-Bot: Deploybot: traffic switch to pool-fallback-2 completed (ID: db-1710661234).
Maya: What I saw on replay: a lot of long-context requests interleaved with many short ones — KV cache gets thrash and we see repeated reclaim cycles. Batching heuristics are coalescing short requests into long sequences which spikes workspace. Recommend clamping batching for rw-api: max_batch_tokens=1024 and bias towards small-batch kernel.
Sanjay: Quick mitigation applied: `rtctl update-route --name rw-api --max-batch-size 4 --batch-token-cap 1024`. Also set `REDWOOD_ALLOC_HEADROOM=0.08` on the pool to reduce eager allocations. Watch for perf regressions.
Li: For kernel side you can nudge selector without restart: `kernel.selector.set_policy --route rw-api --bias memory_friendly=0.75` — that will prefer memory-efficient kernels for short/medium sequences.
OpsOnCall: Telemetry: node r-4-23 shows repeated cudaMalloc failures at 10:18; eviction logs show aggressive KV eviction cycles every ~12s. Keeping traffic on fallback but we need a plan to restore primary.
Alex: Mitigation plan: 1) Keep fallback routing and monitor. 2) Ramp down batching and clamp token coalescing. 3) Adjust allocator: increase soft-reserve to 20MB and decrease eager prefetch. 4) If OOMs persist, enable per-request quick-fail policy for >12k tokens to return 429. 5) Post-incident: tune KV TTL and add short-window adaptive eviction.
Maya: How to toggle soft-reserve: `rtctl set-allocator --soft-reserve 20MB --prefetch-window 0.5s` — recommend apply to pool-fallback-2 first, observe for 5–10m.
Sanjay: Also enabling small incremental KV eviction (staircase): `kvctl set-policy --mode incremental --step 2MB --period 8s` — this should smooth out full-throttle evictions.
Alex: Update after 10m of changes: OOM rate dropped ~85% on the fallback cluster. Suggest progressive traffic shift: move 20% back and watch p50/p95 and OOM counts. I'll capture perf profile and kernel trace for postmortem.
OpsOnCall: Traffic ramp started to 20% at 10:35. No new OOMs observed so far. Holding for another 10m then increase.
Li: FYI there's a perf regression in latest kernel release krel-2.8.1 that increases workspace allocation for fused-attention kernels on short sequences; raised GH issue #3254. If we see re-emergence, consider rollback.
Alex: Good catch. Rollback plan: revert krel-2.8.1 on affected nodes and pin kernel policy to memory_friendly until upstream fix. Trigger condition: >3 OOMs / 5m on restored traffic.
Maya: Postmortem action items I will own: add route-level default for batch token cap (1024), autotune allocator headroom per workload, add KV hot-path telemetry to flag thrash early, and add an automated ramp/fallback checklist to the runbook.
Alex: Thanks all — I'll write a concise incident summary and add exact rtctl/kvctl commands + rollback triggers to the runbook. Closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
